title: Consumer Impatience, Technological Innovation, and Market Structure
eligible_reason: No DiD or event-study design. The paper estimates a structural demand model for pizza delivery (fn_estimation.py) with an IV first stage for price and delivery time (feols(del ~ mgprice + deltime | index + yearweek) and IV variants in fn_iv_.R, continuous regressors, pizzeria and year-week FE), then simulates counterfactual delivery-time reductions and a premium-delivery policy. The 'introduction of a technology that reduces delivery time' in the abstract is a counterfactual simulation, not an observed staggered adoption.
design_notes: Online pizza-delivery order data (anonymized). code_result/fn_iv_.R: Table 3 and A.2-A.3 IV/OLS with pizzeria (index) and yearweek FE, two-way clustering; code_estimation/fn_estimation.py: demand estimation; fn_fe_.R: t-tests of pizzeria FE; counterfactual R scripts. No treatment indicator anywhere in the code (grep for treat/did/event found nothing).

specs.exclusion_reason: continuous regressors, IV; not a DiD

data_files: replication_code/data/data_result/*.csv (df_reg.csv, pizzlist.csv, estimation draws, counterfactual outputs)
software_notes: R (fixest, dplyr) and Python (demand estimation, notebooks).
priority_note: Not eligible: structural/IV design, no staggered adoption.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (readme.txt, fn_iv_.R, fn_fe_.R, grep of all R/py/ipynb).
